blocks.text: Allaah's Name Al-Mu'tee The Giver, is authentically reported in Saheeh Bukhaaree from a hadeeth by Mu'aawiyah who said that the Messenger of Allaah ﷺ said,

"If Allah wants to do good for somebody, he makes him comprehend the Religion (i.e. Islam), and Allah is the Giver and I am Al-Qaasim (i.e. the distributor), and this (Muslim) nation will remain victorious over their opponents, till Allaah's Order comes and they will still be victorious"
Allaah's Name Al-Jawaad The Most Generous is mentioned in a Qudsee Hadeeth by Aboo Dharr who said that the Messenger of Allaah ﷺ said,

"Allaah says, O My servants, all of you are astray except those that I have guided… That is because I am the Most Generous, The Glorious, I do what I want. I give by My speech and I punish by My speech, whenever I want something I only say: "Be" and it is."

Al-Mu'tee The Giver means the One alone who gives in reality. Nothing can prevent Him giving and nothing can give when He prevents. His giving is by speech and His preventing is by speech. If He wishes something He only has to say 'Be' and it is. Everything that a servant has of blessings is from His grace and giving. His giving extends over all His servants – believers and disbelievers, righteous and disobedient. This is in this life, as for the Day of Resurrection He will specifically give to His allies and believers. Allaah said,

Say (O Muhammad): "Who has forbidden the adoration with clothes given by Allah, which He has produced for his slaves, and At-Taiyibat [all kinds of Halal (lawful) things] of food?" Say: "They are, in the life of this world, for those who believe, (and) exclusively for them (believers) on the Day of Resurrection (the disbelievers will not share them)." Thus We explain the Ayat (Islamic laws) in detail for people who have knowledge.

Al-Jawaad The Most Generous means plentiful giving. The One whose generosity covers all created beings. He fills them from His grace, generosity and varied blessings. Nothing created is free from His good treatment for the blinking of an eye.

"Allaah loves for His servants to have hope in Him, to have expectations and to ask Him of His grace. This is because He is the King, the Truth and the Most Generous. He is more generous than what He was asked for and is more expansive than the one who gives. There is nothing more beloved to The Generous than His servants having hope and expectation in Him and for them asking Him. In a hadeeth it states that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, he who does not ask Allah, He becomes angry with him.""
blocks.ref: Ibnul Qayyim, Madaarij as-Saalikeen 1/211-212 (the hadeeth: Tirmidhee 3373; Bukhaaree in Al-Adab al-Mufrad 658)

blocks.text: We hope The Most Generous Al-Jawaad Al-Kareem grants us all the means that lead to gaining His generosity and bounty and that He protects us from the means that lead to His anger, punishment and just revenge. Generosity is His generosity and giving is His giving. The command is His before and after. He has no partner.

keyPoints: Al-Mu'tee is authentically reported in Saheeh Bukhaaree in the hadeeth of Mu'aawiyah: "Allah is the Giver and I am Al-Qaasim (the distributor)."
Al-Jawaad is mentioned in the Qudsee hadeeth of Aboo Dharr: "That is because I am the Most Generous, The Glorious, I do what I want."
Al-Mu'tee means the One alone who gives in reality; nothing can prevent His giving and nothing can give when He prevents, and His giving and preventing are by speech.
His giving in this life extends over all His servants, believers and disbelievers, but on the Day of Resurrection He will specifically give to His allies and believers.
Al-Jawaad means plentiful giving, the One whose generosity covers all created beings; nothing created is free from His good treatment for the blinking of an eye.
Ibnul Qayyim said nothing is more beloved to The Generous than His servants having hope in Him and asking Him; whoever does not ask Allaah, He becomes angry with him.

evidence.text: "...and Allah is the Giver and I am Al-Qaasim (i.e. the distributor)..."
"...That is because I am the Most Generous, The Glorious, I do what I want. I give by My speech and I punish by My speech..."

recall.a: The Giver: the One alone who gives in reality; nothing can prevent Him giving and nothing can give when He prevents.
The Most Generous: plentiful giving, the One whose generosity covers all created beings; nothing created is free from His good treatment for the blinking of an eye.

recall.q: In which hadeeth is Al-Mu'tee reported?
recall.a: The hadeeth of Mu'aawiyah in Saheeh Bukhaaree: "If Allah wants to do good for somebody, he makes him comprehend the Religion... and Allah is the Giver and I am Al-Qaasim."

recall.q: How does Allaah's giving differ between this life and the Day of Resurrection?
recall.a: In this life His giving extends over believers and disbelievers, righteous and disobedient; on the Day of Resurrection He will specifically give to His allies and believers (A'raaf 7:32).

recall.q: According to Ibnul Qayyim, what is most beloved to The Generous?
recall.a: His servants having hope and expectation in Him and asking Him.
